## Research question

A SQL request may reference inaccessible or unavailable tables while other available sources could support a related analytical goal.

## Method

InQuRe filters candidate tables, prompts GPT-4o for diverse SQL alternatives directly or through an inferred natural-language intent, prunes implausible joins, ranks using embedding or LLM similarity with optional MMR, and repairs executability errors.

## Evaluation

The study uses 957 Spider-derived table schemas across 138 domains, ten authored SQL queries and three raters per candidate. Majority judgments define perceived intent preservation. Quality requests five rewrites per query; separate runtime experiments request ten. Runtime measures rewriting components, not execution over populated tables.

## What the results support

LLM-based filtering and intent-mediated rewriting outperform the tested embedding-filter configurations on judged rewrite quality. Failures include unusable joins, omitted constraints and unsuitable proxy attributes. LLM similarity improves ranking at added rewrite cost; schema-based correction does not establish result correctness.

## Limits and qualifications

Different result sets and correlated substitutes are permitted by design, without a formal or empirical semantic-equivalence guarantee. No actual-data answer validation or query-speedup study is reported. One model, ten inputs and sparsely documented rater protocol limit generalization; user-study annotations are not released. Natural-language input is unsupported in the checked code.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

An adjacent source-recovery design showing how an unavailable request can be reformulated. Such proposals should remain distinguishable from answering the original intent, detecting intrinsic unanswerability, or obtaining user approval for changed assumptions.
